subject: Proposal: Usage-anchored slot reallocation for Q4 renewal
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@edgeflux.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@edgeflux.ai
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Usage report & request: slot reallocation ahead of Q4 renewals

Neha,

Quick note — we pulled the Q3 token and inference run logs and theres been a clear shift in distribution: a 28% uptick in long-context generations and a 14% steady increase in concurrent KV cache hotness during peak hours. The attached CSV has a breakdown by route and hourly percentiles.

Were approaching the renewal conversation and want to avoid a blunt commitment increase if we can instead reallocate some slots and add a small thermal buffer for Q4. Specifically asking: can Redwood map 40 dedicated slots into a mixed-slab configuration for Oct–Dec with an option to convert to full reserved GPUs in Jan if utilization stays high?

What we need from you:
- A short feasibility note on mixed-slab vs dedicated slot behavior for long-context models.
- A proposed mapping (which routes to move, expected latency impact).
- Any docs/procurement steps (we may need a PO amendment).

Attachments: edgeflux-usage-q3.csv (CSV)

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform
EdgeFlux.ai

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@edgeflux.ai>
Cc: procurement@edgeflux.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage report & request: slot reallocation ahead of Q4 renewals

Thanks for the data, Sanjay — useful signal. I reviewed the CSV and the percentile shifts you highlighted look real. High-level response below; copying Karthik for sizing and Laura for commercial/PO follow-up.

Short answer: yes, we can offer a mixed-slab configuration as a time-bound mitigation that preserves your renewal flexibility. Itll behave like this in practice:
- Mixed-slab (slot + burst) reduces steady-state committed GPUs but maintains headroom for long-context tails.
- Latency: for the routes with >50% long-context (you have three), expect a 5–12% p95 increase if we dont relocate KV-heavy routes onto dedicated slab. We can avoid >10% increase by moving two routes we identified in the CSV.
- Cost: modeled as an incremental 8% unit-rate vs current committed baseline for Oct–Dec; conversion option in Jan can be a one-click amendment.

Proposed immediate steps:
1) Karthik: quick technical slot mapping and safety buffer (40 slots -> mapping attached).
2) Laura: draft amendment language for a temporary slab mix and PO changes; well include a conversion clause for Jan.
3) Sanjay: confirm the three routes you want prioritized and whether procurement needs a formal SOW.

Ill attach a mapping workbook for your review — this is a short-term operational safety plan, not a long-term commit ask.

Attachments: redwood-slot-mapping-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@edgeflux.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2027 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage report & request: slot reallocation ahead of Q4 renewals

On Thu, Oct 14, 2027 at 1:45 PM neha_kapoor@redwood.com wrote:
> I’ll attach a mapping workbook for your review — this is a short-term operational safety plan, not a long-term commit ask.

Quick technical readout from my side after running a small smoke test in staging with similar load shapes:
- Mapping: we can reassign 40 slots into a 60/40 slot-to-slab mix across two clusters to reduce cross-tenant interference. I described exact route assignments in the attached workbook.
- KV cache: enabling prefix-KV pinning for the two hot routes cuts p95 tail by ~9% in our test; it does consume about 12% more mem per instance.
- Autoscale safety: recommend enabling a burst-capacity rule that caps burst at 25% of slab capacity and a fallback policy to the nearest compatible model variant to avoid request failures during sudden spikes.

Risks/notes:
- If EdgeFlux sees continued growth past Dec, conversion to reserved GPUs is recommended — mixed-slab buys time but is not a substitute for predictable committed capacity when sustained.
- We need a short Ops change window (1 hour) to apply slot mapping and pin KV; preferred maintenance window: Sun 23:00–00:30 PT.

If that works Ill prepare an ops runbook and a short performance note you can share with procurement.

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@edgeflux.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage report & request: slot reallocation ahead of Q4 renewals

Thanks all — summary and next steps below so procurement and execs have a single doc for the renewal thread.

Summary:
- We will provision a temporary mixed-slab configuration: 40 slots reallocated into a 60/40 slot-to-slab mix across two clusters.
- Expected impact: 5–12% p95 increase on non-migrated routes; <5% on prioritized KV-pinned routes.
- Cost delta: ~8% Oct–Dec; conversion option to reserved GPUs available from Jan 1 under the existing pricing schedule.

Operational items (action owners):
- Karthik: prepare ops runbook and schedule maintenance window (requested: Sun 2027-10-17 23:00–00:30 PT).
- Laura: draft a one-page amendment + PO addendum and upload to HubSpot; include conversion clause and pricing table.
- Sanjay: confirm the three routes to prioritize and whether procurement wants the amendment as a PO or SOW.

If procurement signs off, Laura — can you attach the DocuSign link and the PO number here? We can queue the ops change pending PO.

Thanks — Ill follow up Monday with the runbook and performance note.

Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
